newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland Bank sees 1-2 pct Finnish inflation in '98.
newsitem.headline: Finland Bank sees 1-2 pct Finnish inflation in '98.

text.p: Bank of Finland board of management member Mattio Vanhala said on Monday the central bank expected Finnish inflation to rise between one and two percent in 1998.

"We have set our sights on inflation edging up beyond one percent. We see it between one and two percent in 1998," Vanhala told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) in an interview due to be broadcast later this week.
When asked whether a pre-emptive key interest rate hike could be needed amidst strong growth and ahead of the coming incomes settlement talks late this autumn, Vanhala said:
"Everytime we identify an increase in inflation pressures we react with interest rates."
"That is not the case at the moment. If anything, the outlook is as stable as when we last looked," he added.
On January 17, Vanhala said Finnish interest rates were in line with the economic situation and the outlook.
On January 10, the Bank of Finland said inflation looked likely to remain slow.

In January, Finnish consumer prices rose 0.6 percent year-on-year while underlying inflation, a key central bank monetary policy gauge, edged 0.4 percent higher year-on-year in December, Statistics Finland reported on February 14.
